transcript: you were literally *this* close to missing out on one of the biggest hidden gems of the theatre season but luckily you've been given another chance the artist performs the show with his real life mother and the concept is that he's using this performance art to emotionally prepare himself for the day when his mother inevitably passes away so like yes it's kind of morbid but it's also very healing and cathartic and it's this fascinating blend of like physics metaphors with Bengali culture and other ritualistic acts of performance art like by the end of the show you'll probably be crying, but you'll also leave knowing way more about the physics of sand than you ever thought you needed to know but you're gonna love it you're gonna be like “wait, I actually wanted to hear more about the sand!” the show is called Rheology and it was created by Pulitzer finalist Shayok Misha Chowdhury in collaboration with, as I said, his real life mother Bulbul Chakraborty and it was very much a sold out hit when it played it in Brooklyn a couple months ago but even though it was extended it was still a super short run so not very many people got to see it but lucky for you it was just announced that it's coming back next spring at this time at Playwrights Horizons I would really encourage you all to keep your eyes on this after I saw it someone I know texted me being like “is this secretly the best show playing in New York City right now?” and there was certainly a case to be made
reasoning: Creator saw the show during its Brooklyn run and gives an enthusiastic first-hand recommendation, calling it a hidden gem and citing a friend who suggested it might be the best show playing in NYC.
